page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Running head "COMMENTARIUS" and page number "109" at the top. A signature mark "Q 5" at the foot right, and no catchword.

main_text.p: ꝗ[?] Germanis uzz[?], sed, verùm, simile Latinorum ai: lausei[?] Germanis erlosi, libera: tham-ma aruiculus, hoc vel illo: ubilim Germanis ubile:ante, nam, quia: thingardi regnum, quasi kwngardi (quo certè modo legendum putem:) mahs[?] potentia, hodiernis macht: wul-thus quasi Walthus, potentia conjuncta cum gloria, Germanis priscis k walti, hodiernis gewalt: aiwins[?] æternum, sempiternum, idem quod Cimbricum evich, ab ev, Seculum significante, ut ævum Latinorum.

Hæ & alia hoc loco observari possint: quæ arguunt, etsi pleraque Gothica magnopere conveniant cum Alamanicis vel Teutonicis priscis: tamen infinitis quoque vocibus utrosq; inter se discrepare: adeò ut quí vel in omnibus convenientiam investigare, vel omnia Getica sive Gothica ad Teutonicam reducere velit, quod demonstrare nixus est Goropius B canus, ille operam ole-um q; perdere videatur. Hoc certè constat ex utriusque linguæ inter se collatione, Alamanicam sive Teutonicam nostram, cùm superiorem, tum inferiorem, maximâ præstantissimorum & significantissimorum vocabulorum accessione locupletari atque exornari posse.
Hæc de Getis vel Gothis Septentrionalibus.

page.notes: Abbreviated and split words in the Gothic/Greek-looking forms (first glyph, "uzz", "lausei", "mahs", "aiwins", "ubilim", "kwngardi") are doubtful and marked [?]. Print appears to be in a mixed Gothic and roman face in the commentary; these forms are copied as seen. The word "Germanis" beginning the first line and the Greek-like marks may need checking against the scan. The signature "Q 5" is underlined and partly unclear.
